about: Per-model checks added inside a returned <task-result> block. Family names resolve against this file's families, then guidance.json's. Source: the model-traits digest, 'Review lens per model'; evidence IDs are MT-xxx entries. Models with no logged findings get no entry. Rule for a check: a warning about a logged habit plus one small action the coordinator can do from the returned report or with one cheap command (`git status`, `git diff --stat`, run the tests, one grep). Never ask the coordinator to read a transcript, an error trail or a whole diff.

checks.text: It has reported done with the project's tests broken: run them before you accept.
It fixes the reported case and can break a neighbour: run the whole test file, not one case.
If its report mentions added waits or retries for stale data, ask for a fix at the data source instead.
If it stopped over a blocked cleanup, check the main work is finished.
If its report shows only that the error is gone, ask what proves the required result.
It adds test files outside the brief: run `git status` and compare the file list with the brief.
Its own new tests can pass while the project's fail: run the project's tests.
If its report mentions helper agents or a time-out, treat the work as unfinished until you check the result.
It rewrites existing tests to fit its change: run `git diff --stat` and, if an existing test file changed, read that hunk before you trust 'tests pass'.
Most of its failures claimed a passing suite: run the project's tests.
On a wrong displayed value, check with `git diff --stat` that the file that computes the value changed, not only the display file.
At extra high or max effort, if its report mentions helper agents or a time-out, treat the work as unfinished.
Most of its failures claimed a green suite: run the project's tests.
It quits early: if its report says 'did not run', 'partially' or 'incomplete', send the task again.
It has written a test suite that hangs: grep the changed test files for `mock.module` on built-in modules.
Nearly all its failures report done: run the project's tests.
It edits test expectations to fit its code: run `git diff --stat` and read any changed existing test file.
On a wrong displayed value, check with `git diff --stat` that the file that computes the value changed.
It leaves extra files such as findings.md: run `git status` and compare with the brief.
It says done with items missing: match its report against the brief's list of deliverables.
It leaves probes, backups and helper files: run `git status` and look for untracked files.
At low effort on a wrong displayed value, check with `git diff --stat` that the file that computes the value changed.
If it reports a change as already done, open the file and confirm; it trusts git history.
